inherited_risk_from_a3.statement: hive_mind_os.verify.verify_bundle (src/hive_mind_os/verify.py:266-379) re-derives file digests but never reads document['verdict']. A bundle whose verdict is flipped from reject to adopt is ACCEPTED once integrity.json is recomputed, because integrity.json is an unkeyed in-bundle manifest attesting self-consistency rather than authenticity. Any delivery pilot that ships artifacts on the strength of a retained bundle inherits that weakness.

D4.consequence: A grant never goes stale on its own; only the token's own expiry ends it, which puts grant lifetime outside the governance object.
D4.mechanism: src/hive_mind_os/cortex/github/grants.py:91-101 -- DeliveryGrant carries issued_at and no expiry field.
D4.title: DeliveryGrant has issued_at but no expiry

D5.contrast: DeliveryGrant.__post_init__ (grants.py:114-129) DOES recompute its digest over its own fields and raises 'delivery grant digest does not seal its fields' on mismatch. The intent contract should do the same and does not.
D5.mechanism: src/hive_mind_os/brain_kernel/contracts.py:527-535 runs _digest() over intent_digest, which only checks the string looks like a digest. Nothing recomputes it from the intent's contents.
D5.severity: medium -- an intent digest that does not seal its intent is a weak binding
D5.title: EffectIntent.intent_digest is format-checked but never verified to seal its fields

run_summary_retention_decision.reasoning: run-summary.json is the only artifact that aggregates the full 16-call REST list and names the runtime root, so it earns its place. But as the driver emitted it, it paired socket_guard_installed: false with outbound_connection_attempts: 0 and outbound_connection_targets: [] -- counters that belonged to the absent guard and therefore measured nothing. Left as written they read as 'this run made no outbound connections', which is flatly false: a real git push and sixteen REST calls went out.
